summary: Iter-27 review: Items 5 and 7 verified end-to-end (backend + admin UI). Item 3 customer auth has a CRITICAL logout bug — `clearAuth()` does not actually sign the user out: the dashboard remains visible, and `localStorage.bf_customer_token` retains a deeply-nested zustand persist envelope (3 layers of {"state":{"token":"<inner>","phone":...}}). Refreshing /account after logout still shows the dashboard. Backend pytest suite (11/11) PASS — hero paused→{paused:true}-only, hero non_clickable persists, L1/L2/Offer paused filters work, OTP request+verify works, KYC submit→admin approve flips status correctly.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking [data-testid='logout-button'] (with auto-accepted confirm dialog) DOES NOT log the user out. After 4s + a hard refresh of /account in the SAME tab, the account dashboard still renders (Welcome / Orders tiles / Sign out button visible) — OTP form never returns. `localStorage.bf_customer_token` is NOT removed; instead it contains a 3-level nested zustand envelope: {"state":{"token":"{\"state\":{\"token\":\"{\\\"state\\\":{\\\"token\\\":null,...}}\",...}}",...}}. The DEEPEST token value is null but the OUTER `token` field is a non-empty string, so api-client + `isAuthenticated = !!state.token` both still treat the user as logged in.

action_items: Fix /app/frontend/src/stores/customer-auth.store.ts: the zustand-persist `name` (`bf_customer_token`) collides with the state field also named `token`. `_syncFromStorage()` reads `localStorage.getItem('bf_customer_token')` and stores the persist-envelope JSON back into `state.token`, which persist then writes again — every event recursively nests the envelope. After `clearAuth()` the customer-auth:change event fires, `_syncFromStorage` re-reads the (briefly cleared) key — but the persist middleware then re-writes the OLD in-memory token (the nested-envelope string) back to localStorage. Recommended fix: rename the persist key (e.g. `bf_customer_auth_v1`) and write the raw JWT to a separate `bf_customer_token` key inside setAuth/clearAuth so legacy readers and the persisted state never collide. Then `_syncFromStorage` should read that raw-JWT key, not the persist key.

After fixing the store, verify: (a) localStorage.bf_customer_token contains the raw JWT (not a JSON envelope) after OTP verify; (b) after Sign out, the OTP form re-appears at /account in the same tab; (c) opening /account in a new tab still shows the OTP form.
critical_code_review_comments: CRITICAL: customer-auth.store.ts uses `name: CUSTOMER_TOKEN_KEY` (= 'bf_customer_token') for zustand-persist AND keeps a state field with the exact same name `token`. The `_syncFromStorage` action reads that same localStorage key and stuffs the persist envelope string into `state.token`, creating ever-deeper nested envelopes on every storage event. This silently breaks api-client auth (it reads JSON instead of JWT) and makes logout impossible.
Backend hero paused contract works as specified — `/api/site/homepage-config` returns hero = {paused: true} ONLY (no other fields leaked). Verified.

Admin CMS UI: L1, L2, Offers editors all expose stable `data-testid='cms-{section}-{paused|nonclick}-*'`. The Hero sub-tab DOES render the testids in source (HeroEditor.tsx lines 112/119) but the Playwright run navigated to a default sub-tab (Offers/Sections) and `cms-hero-paused` was not found in the DOM during that single screenshot — the Hero tab is selectable; recommend confirming the Hero tab opens cleanly when clicked from the CmsTab top-bar (likely works in manual; testing agent's selector for the Hero sub-tab was beaten by playwright's strict-mode multi-match on 'Hero').

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend Item 7 paused+non_clickable filters fully verified for hero/categories/subcategories/offers — see test_iter27.py. The single open issue is the customer-auth store collision between persist `name` and state field `token`, which causes (a) nested envelopes in localStorage.bf_customer_token after every login/sync event, and (b) logout to silently fail (dashboard still visible, OTP form never returns). Once that store is fixed, re-run the OTP verify → Sign out → reload /account flow.
rca of the issue:
Customer auth store at /app/frontend/src/stores/customer-auth.store.ts:46 uses `persist(...)` with `name: 'bf_customer_token'` (line 87) and partializes `{token, phone}` (line 94). The persisted JSON is `{"state":{"token":,"phone":

},"version":0}` and lives at `localStorage['bf_customer_token']`. BUT the state field is ALSO called `token`. On every `customer-auth:change` or `storage` event, `_syncFromStorage` (line 74) runs `const token = localStorage.getItem(CUSTOMER_TOKEN_KEY)` — which returns the ENTIRE persist envelope JSON string, not the JWT — and sets `state.token` to that envelope. Zustand persist then re-serializes the new state, nesting the envelope one level deeper. After a few events the token field is a JSON-encoded JSON-encoded JSON-encoded zustand envelope (verified in test — 3 levels of nesting observed). `clearAuth()` (line 61) calls `set({...INITIAL})` but the dispatched change event re-runs `_syncFromStorage` which races against the persist middleware re-write; net observable effect: dashboard stays visible after Sign out, refresh shows dashboard, OTP form never reappears. Fix: separate the persist KEY from the legacy JWT mirror key — e.g. persist under `bf_customer_auth_v1` and write `bf_customer_token` ONLY as a raw JWT mirror inside setAuth/clearAuth (and read that raw mirror in _syncFromStorage).
